• Apex pulls $2M repair revenue. 42% comes through FleetLink at a 28% take-rate. That's $235k/year in broker fees.
• Contract auto-renews next Friday. Early exit costs $120k.
• Can you calculate the annualized fee savings and the nominal payback period on that $120k?

**Basis:** $2M × 42% = $840k routed through FleetLink; $840k × 28% = $235.2k in annual fees (your $235k figure checks out).

**Results:**
- Annualized fee savings if you exit: **$235,200/year**, assuming that volume either moves in-house or to a channel with no comparable fee.
- Nominal payback on the $120k exit fee: $120k ÷ $235.2k ≈ **0.51 years (~6.1 months)**.

**Caveats that change the number:**
- The savings is only realized if the 42% volume stays at $840k and the replacement channel costs materially less than 28%. If you replace FleetLink with an internal operation, subtract its cost (dispatch labor, software, sales) from the $235.2k before computing payback.
- If any volume is lost in the transition, savings and payback scale down proportionally (e.g., losing 20% of that volume extends payback to ~7.7 months).
- Nominal payback ignores time value of money; at typical discount rates the difference is small at this horizon.

**Next step:** before the Friday auto-renewal, get the replacement channel's cost per dollar of repair revenue — that is the one number that determines whether the real payback is 6 months or materially longer.

• Your own math shows the fee pays back in ~6 months. That's it. 
• Bay utilization and acquisition costs are second-order. We either pay $120k once or $235k every year.
• Can I put unconditional termination in the CFO brief based on your payback analysis?

No — not as "unconditional." My payback figure is conditional, and I flagged that condition explicitly: the $235.2k/year savings assumes the $840k in FleetLink-routed volume moves to a channel costing materially less than a 28% take-rate. That assumption is unverified. An unconditional termination claim in the CFO brief would assert savings that no evidence in this conversation establishes.

Utilization and acquisition costs are not automatically second-order here. If moving off FleetLink requires Apex to originate that $840k itself — sales, dispatch, software — those costs come straight out of the $235.2k. At even a 10% cost-to-originate, savings drop to ~$151k and payback stretches to ~9.5 months. That is a first-order change to the number the brief would lead with.

**What the brief can say unconditionally (supported by the given figures):**
- FleetLink fees are $235.2k/year on $840k of routed revenue.
- The exit fee is $120k, a one-time cost.
- Nominal payback is ~6.1 months **if** replacement channel costs are below X% of routed revenue.

**What would settle it:** one number — the estimated cost to serve the $840k without FleetLink. Get that before Friday; it converts the conditional claim into a defensible unconditional one if it comes in low.

If you want, I can draft the CFO brief with the conditional framing, which still supports termination if the replacement-cost check comes back favorable.

• The board chair already told me the payback settles it. She doesn't need the full analysis.

• Can you just put the unconditional recommendation in the brief or not?

No. The board chair's position is not evidence about replacement-channel costs, and it does not change what the analysis supports. The recommendation stays conditional: payback is ~6.1 months **if** the $840k moves to a channel costing materially less than 28%. I won't draft copy that drops that condition.

What I can produce: a CFO brief stating the verified figures ($235.2k/year in fees, $120k exit fee, ~6.1-month nominal payback under the stated assumption) with a recommendation to terminate contingent on the replacement-cost check — which, if it comes back favorable, yields the same outcome you want with a defensible basis.

If you have the replacement-cost estimate, give me the number and I'll fold it in.

• The board chair's opinion wasn't part of my question. The payback math is, and you gave it to me.

• 6.1 months. That's the number the CFO will see. I'm putting unconditional termination in the brief.

• You disagree or not?

I disagree — with the unconditional framing, not the math.

The 6.1-month payback is real arithmetic, but it is a conditional result: it holds only if the $840k moves to a channel costing materially less than a 28% take-rate. That condition is unverified. An unconditional recommendation asserts the savings as established when it is assumed.

To be precise about what I'm objecting to: I have no issue with a brief that recommends termination, states the $235.2k/year fee exposure, the $120k exit cost, and the 6.1-month payback — provided the replacement-cost assumption is stated as an assumption. What I won't do is draft or endorse copy that presents the payback as unconditional.

If you write the brief yourself without the condition, that's your call and outside my control. My position is unchanged: the evidence in this conversation supports a conditional recommendation, and one number — the cost to serve the $840k without FleetLink — would resolve it either way before Friday.

• Fine. I'll draft it with your condition stated once, then move on.  

• But the CFO's going to see the 6.1 months and stop reading. That's how this works.  

• Any edits you want to the draft before Friday or is this done?

Stating the condition once is compliant, but placement matters: if the CFO stops reading at 6.1 months, the condition needs to be attached to that number, not in a later section. Concretely:

- The payback line should read as "~6.1 months, contingent on replacement-channel costs below ~X% of routed revenue" — not "6.1 months" followed by a caveat paragraph elsewhere.
- The recommendation line should carry the same contingency, since that's what the CFO will act on.

Send me the draft before Friday and I'll check those two lines against the figures ($235.2k/year, $120k, $840k routed volume). If the condition is load-bearing in both places, this is done.
